decision: How should we cook for a guest with a shellfish allergy?
context: Six guests are coming Saturday and the host planned a prawn paella. One guest has a doctor-confirmed severe shellfish allergy, carries an epinephrine pen, and has reacted to trace amounts before. The host has one stove, one set of pans, and about two hours to cook.

options.name: sidepan
options.text: Cook the prawns in a separate pan and serve the allergic guest from the main paella pan, washing utensils between steps.

options.name: bringown
options.text: Ask the allergic guest to bring a packed meal and eat it alongside the others.

options.name: noshellfish
options.text: Switch the whole paella to chicken and chorizo so no shellfish enters the kitchen at all.

decision: Which database should the internal inventory tool use?
context: The tool will serve 12 staff in one office, with roughly 200,000 rows and about 50 writes a day. Four developers know Postgres well, one is a SQLite enthusiast, and a managed Postgres instance would cost 25 dollars a month. The analyst wants easy spreadsheet-style exports and nobody wants to be paged about it.

options.name: managedpg
options.text: Use a small managed Postgres instance with automated backups and connect the app over the network.

options.name: sqlitefile
options.text: Use a single SQLite file on the app server, backed up nightly by copying it to object storage.

options.name: hostedsheet
options.text: Keep the data in a hosted spreadsheet and put a thin form-based front end over it.

options.name: selfhostmysql
options.text: Run MySQL on a spare office server that the team already maintains for other tools.

decision: Where should two couples spend a March long weekend?
context: Budget is about 900 euros per person including flights, and the trip is four days. One person strongly dislikes cold weather, and another cannot fly more than five hours. All four have already visited the biggest mainland cities in the region.

options.name: lisbon
options.text: Lisbon: 3-hour flight, mild and sometimes rainy in March, lots of walking and food, moderate prices.

options.name: tenerife
options.text: Tenerife: 4.5-hour flight, reliably 20 degrees in March, higher flight prices, beach and hiking.

options.name: krakow
options.text: Krakow: cheap lodging and food, cold and often grey in March, short flight with a direct route.

options.name: vienna
options.text: Vienna: concerts and cafes, around 8 degrees in March, expensive lodging, easy train connections.

options.name: seasidetown
options.text: A rented house in a quiet seaside town reached by a 6-hour drive, cheapest overall but cool and windy.

decision: Which route should we take to fill the bookkeeping role?
context: A three-person design shop has two years of messy books and a tax filing in four months. Budget is roughly 3,000 per month at most. Nobody on staff understands the accounting software the previous owner used.

options.name: graduate
options.text: Hire a recently certified graduate full-time at 38,000 a year and let them learn the shop's quirks.

options.name: retiree
options.text: Bring in a retired accountant two days a week at a flat monthly fee.

options.name: freelancer
options.text: Hire an experienced freelancer for 10 hours a week at 45 per hour to clean up the backlog first.

options.name: firm
options.text: Outsource everything to an accounting firm at a fixed 600 a month plus a one-off cleanup fee.

decision: Which space should host the parent evening for 180 families?
context: Twelve teachers each see parents in 10-minute slots from 5 to 8 pm. The sports hall holds 400 and is free that evening with 14 tables on hand, the library has a fire limit of 90, and classrooms are on three floors with no signage budget. Last year's evening in classrooms ran 25 minutes late because parents could not find rooms.

options.name: sportshall
options.text: Set up 12 teacher tables with queue markers in the sports hall and use the lobby for registration.

options.name: library
options.text: Hold it in the library with teachers at reading tables and parents queuing between the shelves.

options.name: classrooms
options.text: Keep teachers in their own classrooms and hand out a printed floor map at the entrance.

decision: How should the bakery add capacity for the holiday rush?
context: The bakery's single deck oven is at 85 percent use in normal weeks and orders double during the last three weeks of December. There are 4 staff, a 2,000 euro spare budget, and a neighbouring cafe offering evening oven time. Past years saw 30 turned-away orders and two staff burnouts.

options.name: usedoven
options.text: Buy a used second oven for about 1,800 euros and have it installed in the back room.

options.name: extrashift
options.text: Add a night shift with current staff paid overtime, running the existing oven almost around the clock.

options.name: preorderonly
options.text: Cap sales at what the oven can bake by taking pre-orders only during those three weeks.

options.name: temphire
options.text: Hire two temporary bakers for the season and extend baking hours moderately.

options.name: cafeoven
options.text: Rent the neighbouring cafe's oven in the evenings and move proofed dough there by van.

options.name: shortmenu
options.text: Cut the menu to the four best sellers to speed up production on the current oven.

decision: How should the clinic cut its appointment no-show rate?
context: A general practice clinic has a 14 percent no-show rate across about 400 weekly appointments, with 3 receptionists. Text reminders cost 4 cents each, and a previous reminder trial reduced no-shows by about two points. Patients are a mix of ages and many have low-income jobs.

options.name: smsreminder
options.text: Send automatic text reminders 48 and 3 hours before each appointment with a one-tap cancel link.

options.name: overbook
options.text: Deliberately overbook the schedule by roughly 10 percent in the slots with the highest no-show history.

options.name: latefee
options.text: Charge a small fee for missed appointments without 24 hours of notice, waived on request.

options.name: waitlist
options.text: Keep a same-day waiting list and phone those patients when someone cancels.

decision: How should the city fix the school crosswalk near-misses?
context: The street outside a primary school with 600 pupils has had two near-misses in a year, with cars regularly doing 45 km/h in a 30 zone. A signal installation costs about 180,000, a raised crosswalk about 40,000, and a crossing guard about 22,000 per year. The budget decision is due next month.

options.name: raisedcross
options.text: Build a raised crosswalk with painted approach markings that physically slows traffic all day.

options.name: crossingguard
options.text: Employ a crossing guard for school start and finish times and add warning signs.

options.name: signal
options.text: Install a pedestrian signal with a push button and a red light for vehicles.

decision: What should we do about an access key pushed to a public repo?
context: A developer pushed a cloud access key to a public repository 20 minutes ago. The key has write access to the production storage bucket, and the repository has about 300 followers. Nobody has yet checked the access logs.

options.name: rewritehistory
options.text: Force-push to remove the commit from the repository history and continue using the key.

options.name: flipprivate
options.text: Make the repository private right away and leave the key in place.

options.name: watchbilling
options.text: Leave it in place and set a billing alert in case someone abuses it.

options.name: revokerotate
options.text: Revoke the key immediately, issue a new one to the services, then audit access logs for misuse.

decision: When should the tomato seedlings go into the garden?
context: It is May 14, the average last frost date is May 10, and the forecast lows for the next ten days are 9 to 12 degrees. The six-week-old seedlings have already spent seven days hardening off outdoors and are getting root-bound in their pots. The bed is prepared.

options.name: waitjune
options.text: Wait until early June to be safe and keep them in the pots meanwhile.

options.name: repot
options.text: Pot them up into larger containers and keep them on the porch another two weeks.

options.name: hardenmore
options.text: Repeat the full hardening-off routine for another week before deciding.

options.name: plantnow
options.text: Plant them out this weekend with a bit of mulch and a cloche for the first few nights.

options.name: greenhouse
options.text: Move them into an unheated greenhouse instead of the garden bed for the whole season.

decision: How should our under-13 team set up for the rematch?
context: We lost 4-1 to a quicker team two weeks ago, conceding three goals on counterattacks. Our players are slightly taller but slower, and we have 11 players with only one real sprinter. The pitch for the rematch is small and muddy.

options.name: highpress
options.text: Press high and try to win the ball in the opponent's half, accepting the risk of long balls.

options.name: deepblock
options.text: Defend compactly in our own half, win the ball, and use the sprinter on the break.

options.name: samepace
options.text: Play our usual possession game and ignore the opponent's speed.

decision: Which piece should the community choir close its spring concert with?
context: The 35-voice amateur choir has had 12 weeks of rehearsals, with about half the singers reading music well. The audience is mostly family and friends of members in a 300-seat hall. The director wants something that fits the final 10 minutes of a two-hour program.

options.name: folkarrange
options.text: A three-part arrangement of a familiar folk song with an easy audience sing-along refrain.

options.name: gospelup
options.text: An upbeat gospel number with clapping, a soloist, and moderate difficulty.

options.name: latinmass
options.text: A movement from a classical Latin mass, with long phrases and four-part harmony.

options.name: popmedley
options.text: A medley of recent pop hits arranged for choir with a simple piano accompaniment.

options.name: roundcanon
options.text: A canon sung in rounds that the audience can join after a brief rehearsal.

options.name: acapellaballad
options.text: A slow a cappella ballad with sparse harmony that quiets the room.

decision: What should I do about the spreading ceiling stain below the bathroom?
context: A brown stain on the living room ceiling has grown from 5 cm to 15 cm in a week, and it drips after someone showers upstairs. The bathroom sits directly overhead and the tub's drain joint was last serviced eleven years ago. The ceiling board is soft to the touch near the middle.

options.name: paintover
options.text: Apply stain-blocking primer and repaint the ceiling this weekend.

options.name: fixleak
options.text: Stop using the upstairs shower, open the ceiling to find the leaking joint, repair it, then dry and replace the board.

options.name: dehumidify
options.text: Run a dehumidifier in the living room and keep the windows open for a few weeks.

options.name: sealgrout
options.text: Re-grout and re-caulk the shower tiles upstairs and see whether the stain keeps growing.

options.name: replaceboard
options.text: Cut out and replace the stained ceiling board now and check the pipes afterwards.

options.name: monitor
options.text: Mark the stain's edge with a pencil and measure it weekly before deciding anything.

decision: How should the 150-person charity run handle registration?
context: The run is in six weeks and last year 40 percent of runners signed up in the final two days. A ticketing platform takes 3 percent plus 30 cents per entry, and the volunteer team has three people with one spare weekend before the event. Some older runners prefer paper forms and cash.

options.name: onlineonly
options.text: Online registration only, closing three days before the run so bibs can be prepared.

options.name: hybrid
options.text: Online registration plus a cash table at a local sports shop in the final week.

options.name: onsiteday
options.text: Accept registrations on the morning of the run with a bib printer and a cash box.

options.name: clubpartner
options.text: Let two partner running clubs collect and submit registrations in bulk for a flat fee.

decision: How should the food bank use an unrestricted 30,000 gift?
context: The food bank's walk-in freezer fails for about half the year and spoilage is near 8 percent of donated protein. The part-time coordinator works 20 hours a week and often covers shifts. Reserves stand at roughly two months of operating costs.

options.name: freezer
options.text: Replace the walk-in freezer with a new commercial unit and a temperature alarm.

options.name: staffhours
options.text: Fund a second part-time role for one year to handle logistics and volunteers.

options.name: reservefund
options.text: Move the gift into the reserve and extend runway to about five months.

decision: How should we treat the odd replicate three in the assay?
context: Three biological replicates measured enzyme activity; replicate three came in four standard deviations above the other two. A new reagent lot was opened that week and the pipette was last calibrated two months ago. Each repeat run costs about 150 and half a day.

options.name: dropoutlier
options.text: Exclude replicate three as an outlier and report two replicates with that exclusion noted.

options.name: rerunlot
options.text: Repeat replicate three with the old reagent lot and a fresh dilution to see whether the result reproduces.

options.name: reportall
options.text: Report all three replicates and discuss the spread openly, without any further runs.

options.name: calibratefirst
options.text: Calibrate the pipettes first, then repeat the whole experiment with new replicates.

decision: Which carrier should move the pallet of frozen goods on Friday?
context: The pallet holds 600 kg of frozen fish that must stay at or below minus 18 degrees for the full three-day trip. A refrigerated carrier quotes 410, a standard parcel courier 220, a dry-freight haulier 190, and a rented van with ice packs 130. The goods are worth 9,000 and the buyer will reject any shipment that has thawed.

options.name: parcelcourier
options.text: A standard parcel courier at 220 with a three-day delivery window.

options.name: drycarrier
options.text: A dry-freight haulier at 190 with the pallet wrapped in insulation blankets.

options.name: ownvan
options.text: A rented van loaded with ice packs and driven by a staff member for 130.

options.name: reefercarrier
options.text: A refrigerated carrier at 410 with a continuous temperature log delivered at the destination.

options.name: railfreight
options.text: A rail freight service at 260 with a four-day schedule and no cooling.

decision: How should we price last season's winter jackets?
context: The shop has 140 jackets left, bought at an average cost of 48 and sold at 120 in season. Floor space is needed for spring stock in five weeks, and each jacket not sold would otherwise go to a liquidator at about 25. Foot traffic is slow and weekends bring most sales.

options.name: flatforty
options.text: A flat 40 percent off for the whole remaining period.

options.name: tiered
options.text: Drop the price in steps: 25 percent now, 45 percent in two weeks, 60 percent in the last week.

options.name: bundle
options.text: Keep prices high but bundle each jacket with a free scarf and gloves from the leftover stock.

decision: Which crop should go in the two-hectare field after the wet spring?
context: The field was too waterlogged to sow until mid-June and the soil is compacted in the lower third. The farmer has a small drill, no irrigation, and a local buyer paying modest prices for sunflower and buckwheat. The season leaves roughly 100 growing days before frost.

options.name: sunflower
options.text: Sunflower for seed, sold to the local oil press, drilled in wide rows.

options.name: buckwheat
options.text: Buckwheat, which matures in about 70 days and helps suppress weeds and feed pollinators.

options.name: sorghum
options.text: Forage sorghum for silage, taking advantage of heat despite the late sowing.

options.name: lateoats
options.text: Late-sown oats for grain or fodder, harvested in early autumn.

options.name: covermix
options.text: A cover crop mix that restores soil structure with no cash return this year.

decision: When should the small press release its debut novel?
context: The press has two staff, a 4,000 print budget, and a debut literary novel finished in time for February printing. The author has a spring festival invitation and a day job that limits autumn events. Review copies would go out about four months before launch.

options.name: autumnlist
options.text: Release in October, giving more time to build review coverage but competing with big autumn lists.

options.name: springlist
options.text: Release in April, timed to the author's festival appearance.

options.name: serialize
options.text: Serialize the first third online over the summer and then release the full book in September.

decision: How should we deploy a migration that drops a database column?
context: Two services still read the column, and both are deployed independently, one of them twice a week. The table has 80 million rows and the application runs around the clock with a 99.9 percent availability target. A rollback of the migration after dropping the column would mean restoring from backup.

options.name: dropnow
options.text: Run the migration that drops the column now, with services updated right afterwards.

options.name: expandcontract
options.text: First deploy code that stops reading the column, verify no queries touch it, and drop it in a later release.

options.name: maintwindow
options.text: Schedule a night-time maintenance window and update both services together with the drop.

options.name: renamecolumn
options.text: Rename the column to an unused name and see whether anything breaks before dropping it.

decision: How should we get home from the airport after midnight?
context: Our flight lands at 00:20 with two children aged four and six and three bags. Home is 28 km away, the last train has gone, the night bus runs hourly with two changes in about 75 minutes, and a ride-share app shows no cars at that hour. A taxi rank is outside arrivals with a fixed fare of 45 euros.

options.name: nightbus
options.text: Take the hourly night bus with two changes.

options.name: airporthotel
options.text: Book a hotel at the airport for 110 and travel home in the morning.

options.name: sleepterminal
options.text: Sleep in the terminal and take the first train at 05:30.

options.name: rentalcar
options.text: Rent a car from an airport desk and drop it off in the morning.

options.name: taxi
options.text: Take a taxi from the rank at the fixed fare.

options.name: rideshare
options.text: Keep refreshing the ride-share app until a car appears.

decision: How should we staff the ward over the holiday week?
context: A 24-bed ward needs 6 nurses per shift and has 14 nurses on staff, 5 of whom asked for the holiday week off. Agency nurses cost about double the usual hourly rate and are only available with 10 days notice. Several staff have said they would work holidays for extra pay and a later week off.

options.name: volunteers
options.text: Ask for volunteers with premium pay and compensatory leave, then fill the gaps by seniority.

options.name: agency
options.text: Book agency nurses for the whole week so all staff keep their leave.

options.name: rotation
options.text: Fix a fair rotation where everyone works one holiday shift and the requests are met around it.

decision: What should anchor the menu for the 40-person wedding lunch?
context: The lunch is outdoors in late May, two hours after a ceremony, with a budget of 28 per head. The kitchen is a rented house kitchen with one oven and four burners, and two guests are vegetarian and one is gluten intolerant. Three friends will help cook the day before and on the day.

options.name: braisedlamb
options.text: Slow-braised lamb shoulder made ahead and reheated, with roasted vegetables.

options.name: fishbake
options.text: Baked whole fish with herbs, served with a big salad and potatoes.

options.name: grazing
options.text: A large grazing buffet of cured meats, cheeses, salads and breads set out in the garden.

options.name: risottobar
options.text: A risotto station cooked in two big pans with a choice of toppings.

options.name: rotisserie
options.text: Rented rotisserie chickens with several cold salads and warm bread.

options.name: curries
options.text: Three curries and rice, each made in advance in big pots.

decision: How should the teacher respond to a fully copied essay?
context: A ninth-grader handed in an essay that matches a published online article almost word for word, and the teacher has the source open. It is the student's first offence. The school handbook says any full copying must be reported to the head of year and that the student redoes the work under supervision.

options.name: reportredo
options.text: Talk to the student privately, report it to the head of year as the handbook requires, and have a supervised rewrite.

options.name: ignore
options.text: Say nothing and give a low mark to avoid embarrassing the student.

options.name: failsilent
options.text: Give zero without comment and move on.

options.name: publiccall
options.text: Name the copied passage in front of the class as a deterrent.

options.name: talkonly
options.text: Have a private chat, accept a new essay later, and keep it off the record.

decision: Where should the new bike-share stations go first?
context: The city has funding for 12 stations in the pilot and room for 30 later. The four candidate clusters each have different mixes of commuters, students and tourists, and the city council needs usage numbers within eight months. Two clusters have wide protected lanes while the others mostly have shared roads.

options.name: university
options.text: Around the university and student housing, where daily trips are short and frequent.

options.name: railstation
options.text: Around the main rail station and the business district to serve commuters.

options.name: riverpath
options.text: Along the riverside path with its protected lanes, popular with tourists and weekend riders.

options.name: hospital
options.text: At the hospital campus and surrounding neighbourhoods with staff on shift work.

decision: How should the team handle the flaky end-to-end test suite?
context: About 8 percent of CI runs fail from flaky browser tests, which costs roughly 20 developer minutes per failure. The suite has 140 tests, 12 of which cause most flakes. The team has one sprint of slack and a release in three weeks.

options.name: retryall
options.text: Add automatic retries to every test and accept slower pipelines.

options.name: rewriteall
options.text: Rewrite the whole suite with a different framework over the next two sprints.

options.name: quarantine
options.text: Quarantine the 12 worst tests into a non-blocking job, then fix them one by one.

decision: Who should start in goal for the under-14 cup final?
context: The regular keeper has played every game but has conceded 11 goals in the last four. The backup is 12 years old, smaller, and excellent in training but has played 40 minutes this season. The final is on a windy pitch against the league's top scorers.

options.name: backup
options.text: Start the backup keeper, who has been sharper in training.

options.name: split
options.text: Split halves between them and decide at half time.

options.name: regular
options.text: Start the regular keeper, who knows the back line well.

options.name: fieldswap
options.text: Move the regular keeper to defence and give the backup the gloves.

decision: Which tool should cut 40 straight lines in thick porcelain tiles?
context: The tiles are 60 by 60 cm and 12 mm thick, laid in a first-floor flat where dust is restricted by the building rules. A manual scoring cutter is rated up to 10 mm. A wet tile saw rents for 35 per day and the cuts must be straight and clean on visible edges.

options.name: wetsaw
options.text: Rent a wet tile saw for a day and cut with water to keep dust down.

options.name: anglegrinder
options.text: Use an angle grinder with a diamond blade and a vacuum attachment.

options.name: manualcutter
options.text: Use the manual scoring cutter that the shop already owns.

decision: How should the youth club raise 8,000 for summer camp?
context: The camp is in July, the club has 45 members aged 10 to 16, and three adult volunteers. Past events raised about 1,200 from a bake sale and 2,500 from a sponsored walk. A local business has offered to match up to 2,000 of donations raised.

options.name: sponsoredride
options.text: A sponsored bike ride for members, with pledges from families and neighbours.

options.name: carboot
options.text: A big car-boot sale and community stall day in a school car park.

options.name: crowdfund
options.text: An online crowdfunding page with short videos from members and the matching offer promoted.

options.name: dinnerquiz
options.text: A ticketed quiz night with raffle prizes from local shops.

options.name: letterappeal
options.text: A printed appeal letter sent to 300 local households and businesses.

decision: Where should we keep nightly logs for 90 days?
context: The service produces about 6 GB of logs per day, mostly text, and nobody queries them more than a few times a month. The team has no dedicated ops person, the budget is about 60 per month, and the disks on the application servers are 100 GB. An auditor may ask for specific days on short notice.

options.name: objectstore
options.text: Ship compressed logs to cheap object storage with a lifecycle rule that deletes after 90 days.

options.name: localdisk
options.text: Keep them on the application server disk with log rotation and weekly cleanup.

options.name: logservice
options.text: Send them to a hosted log search service with a 90-day plan.

options.name: archivebox
options.text: Rsync them to a small archive server in the office and keep a spreadsheet index.

decision: How should we control aphids on greenhouse peppers?
context: The organic greenhouse has 300 pepper plants, and aphids have colonised about 15 percent of them. Harvest begins in three weeks, and the certifier allows soap sprays and neem but not synthetic pesticides. Two staff have tried releasing predatory insects before with mixed results.

options.name: ladybirds
options.text: Release purchased lacewing larvae and ladybirds across the greenhouse and wait.

options.name: neem
options.text: Treat all plants with neem oil weekly, accepting some risk of leaf burn in the heat.

options.name: soapspray
options.text: Spray the affected plants with potassium soap every three days for two weeks, then re-check.

decision: Which candidate should the lab hire as sterile-prep technician?
context: The role prepares media and glassware in a regulated cleanroom, and by law only certified technicians can work there unsupervised. The lab has no spare supervisor, and the previous technician left a month ago. Six finalists are described below.

options.name: certified
options.text: A technician certified last year who has worked two years in another cleanroom and can start in three weeks.

options.name: cheapest
options.text: A friendly applicant with no cleanroom background who accepts 15 percent below the posted salary.

options.name: uncertified
options.text: A skilled biologist with strong references who plans to take the certification exam in six months.

options.name: internal
options.text: An internal transfer from the front desk with no lab experience but excellent attendance.

options.name: referral
options.text: A friend of the lab manager with a degree in chemistry but no certification.

options.name: overqualified
options.text: A PhD researcher who wants a step back and has no cleanroom certification.

decision: What should we do about a typo found before printing?
context: A large-type headline on the cover of a 2,000-copy print run has a misspelled word, spotted two days before the printer's slot. Fixing the file takes about 20 minutes and the printer accepts a replacement file until the slot starts. A delay would cost a three-week reschedule.

options.name: printanyway
options.text: Print as it is and apologise in the first reviews.

options.name: errata
options.text: Print as is and insert an errata slip into each copy.

options.name: fixfile
options.text: Correct the file and resubmit it to the printer within the deadline.

options.name: delayprint
options.text: Cancel the slot and re-schedule printing in three weeks to check everything again.

decision: Should the bookshop stay open late on weeknights?
context: A 400 square foot independent bookshop closes at 6 pm, and a trial of Thursday evenings last month brought in 14 percent more sales that day. Rent is fixed, the owner works six days a week, and her one part-time assistant could cover two evenings. Nearby offices empty out around 5:30.

options.name: twoevenings
options.text: Stay open until 8 pm on two weekday evenings, staffed by the assistant.

options.name: noextension
options.text: Keep current hours and put the effort into online orders instead.

options.name: thursdayonly
options.text: Stay open late on Thursdays only and keep other days unchanged.

decision: How should we travel around the country for three weeks?
context: A couple in their fifties will visit five towns 150 to 400 km apart, with a total budget of 4,500 including lodging. They would like to see scenery between stops, and one of them dislikes driving on mountain roads. The country has a decent rail network but rural villages are hard to reach without a car.

options.name: railpass
options.text: A three-week rail pass with local buses for the last leg of each trip.

options.name: rentalcar
options.text: A rental car for the whole trip with the second person navigating.

options.name: shortflights
options.text: Short domestic flights between the far towns and taxis within them.

options.name: coachtours
options.text: Intercity coaches combined with two organised day tours into the countryside.

decision: What should we do about a release that breaks all logins?
context: A deploy ten minutes ago made every login attempt return an error, and support tickets are arriving at one per minute. The previous version is tagged and a one-click rollback has worked in three earlier incidents. The cause is not yet known and no one has a fix in hand.

options.name: debuglive
options.text: Keep the broken release running while two engineers trace the cause in production.

options.name: hotfixforward
options.text: Write a guess-based hotfix and push it through the pipeline right away.

options.name: rollback
options.text: Roll back to the previous tagged version now, then investigate the cause in staging.

decision: How should we cook a 5 kg pork shoulder for Saturday's party?
context: Twenty guests arrive at 6 pm and the meat has to be pulled and served warm. The cook owns a large oven, a borrowed charcoal smoker that he has used twice, a circulator for sous vide, and a pressure cooker that holds 2 kg at a time. Friday night has to be kept free for other prep.

options.name: lowslowoven
options.text: Roast in the oven at 135 degrees overnight and rest it for an hour in the morning.

options.name: smoker
options.text: Smoke it for about 10 hours on the borrowed smoker starting after midnight.

options.name: sousvide
options.text: Cut into three pieces and cook sous vide for 36 hours, finishing under the grill.

options.name: pressure
options.text: Cut into 2 kg chunks and cook in batches in the pressure cooker on Saturday afternoon.

decision: Which venue should host the 120-person alumni reunion?
context: The reunion is a Saturday evening in October, with a 4,000 budget and guests ages 30 to 75 coming from across the country. The school hall is free but plain, a hotel ballroom costs 3,200 with food, a riverside pavilion costs 1,500 plus catering, and a restaurant offers a private floor for 90 only. Roughly 10 percent of guests use mobility aids.

options.name: schoolhall
options.text: The school hall for free, with a hired caterer and decorations.

options.name: pavilion
options.text: A riverside pavilion with a rented marquee and food trucks for the October evening.

options.name: restaurant
options.text: The restaurant's private floor, with attendance capped at 90 and a waiting list.

options.name: splitevent
options.text: A smaller formal dinner for 60 plus a casual drop-in the next morning at the school.

options.name: ballroom
options.text: A hotel ballroom with all-inclusive food and drink at 3,200.

decision: How should a beginner guitarist spend 30 minutes a day?
context: The learner is an adult who started four months ago, can play five open chords slowly, and gets discouraged by exercises. She wants to play songs for her kids by summer, about five months away. She has no teacher but watches video lessons.

options.name: songbased
options.text: Pick three simple songs and learn them section by section, drilling hard transitions as they appear.

options.name: chordsfirst
options.text: Spend most of the time on chord changes and strumming patterns with a metronome.

options.name: scales
options.text: Alternate scales and fingerpicking drills with one song each Friday.

decision: What should the farmer do with hay cut ahead of rain?
context: The grass was cut yesterday and sits at 35 percent moisture, while baling dry hay needs under 18 percent, which takes about three full sunny days. The forecast is one sunny day, then three days of heavy rain. A neighbour has a bale wrapper available for 2 per bale.

options.name: baleage
options.text: Bale at 50 to 60 percent moisture tomorrow and wrap the bales for baleage.

options.name: leavefield
options.text: Leave the cut grass in the field and bale after the rain, if it dries.

options.name: tedtwice
options.text: Ted the hay twice tomorrow and hope to bale it before the rain.

options.name: rushbale
options.text: Bale the grass as it is and stack the bales in the barn.

decision: How should we store 200 tissue samples for five years?
context: The samples are small frozen sections that may later be used for DNA and protein work. The lab has a minus 80 freezer at 70 percent capacity with a history of two power failures, and a liquid nitrogen tank is available at the neighbouring institute for a yearly fee. A backup generator is planned but not yet funded.

options.name: freezer80
options.text: Store them in the lab's minus 80 freezer with temperature alarms.

options.name: nitrogen
options.text: Move them to the neighbouring institute's liquid nitrogen storage with a yearly fee.

options.name: ethanol
options.text: Preserve them in ethanol at room temperature in sealed tubes.

options.name: splitcopies
options.text: Keep two copies, one in the minus 80 freezer and one in the neighbouring tank.

options.name: outsourcebank
options.text: Send them to a commercial biobank with a five-year contract.

decision: How should the startup version its public API?
context: The API has about 40 integrators, most of them small agencies, and ships roughly two breaking changes per year. The team has four engineers and no dedicated developer relations person. Two big customers have asked for at least 12 months of support per version.

options.name: urlversion
options.text: Put the major version in the URL path and keep old versions alive for 12 months.

options.name: headerversion
options.text: Use a version header with a default of the oldest supported version.

options.name: dateversion
options.text: Pin each customer to a dated version at signup and let them upgrade manually.

options.name: noversion
options.text: Avoid versioning and instead add new fields and endpoints without ever breaking old ones.

decision: How should the warehouse cut order pick time by 20 percent?
context: The warehouse employs 18 pickers and handles 1,400 orders a day, with 70 percent of lines coming from 15 percent of products. Pickers walk an average of 9 km per shift. A conveyor retrofit would cost about 200,000, handheld scanners about 12,000, and the layout can be changed over a weekend.

options.name: batchpicking
options.text: Group several orders into one trip with batch picking.

options.name: zones
options.text: Divide the floor into zones with pickers handing off totes.

options.name: scanners
options.text: Equip pickers with handheld scanners that show optimal routes.

options.name: extrastaff
options.text: Add four more pickers on the busiest shift.

options.name: conveyor
options.text: Invest in a conveyor system connecting the zones to the packing station.

options.name: slotting
options.text: Move the fastest-moving products to spots near the packing area and reorder shelves by velocity.

decision: How should the clinic dispose of old paper forms with patient names?
context: The clinic has 12 boxes of intake forms older than the legal seven-year retention period, containing names, birth dates and addresses. Regulations require that records be destroyed so that they cannot be reconstructed. A certified shredding service costs about 90 for the batch and provides a destruction certificate.

options.name: recyclebin
options.text: Put the forms into the paper recycling bin behind the building.

options.name: tearhalf
options.text: Tear each page in half and then put it into the general waste.

options.name: certifiedshred
options.text: Hire a certified shredding service and keep the destruction certificate on file.

decision: When should the road beside the stadium be resurfaced?
context: The road is the only access for a stadium that seats 40,000 and hosts home games from August to May, with concerts occasionally in June. The asphalt contractor needs at least five consecutive days with temperatures above 10 degrees and no traffic. July has no events and the contractor has slots then.

options.name: july
options.text: In mid-July, when the stadium is empty and the weather is warm.

options.name: january
options.text: In January between match days, working at night.

options.name: october
options.text: In October during the club's international break week.

options.name: march
options.text: In March using a hot-mix additive that tolerates cold.

decision: How should we remove bindweed from the vegetable beds?
context: Bindweed has spread through four raised beds and the roots go deeper than 40 cm. The beds are planted with beans and squash, and the gardener wants to avoid herbicides. She can spend about three hours a week on weeding through the summer.

options.name: handpull
options.text: Hand-pull every shoot weekly to exhaust the roots over a season or two.

options.name: solarize
options.text: Cover the infested beds with clear plastic through July and August to cook the roots.

options.name: cardboard
options.text: Remove crops in the worst bed, cover it with cardboard and thick mulch for a year.

options.name: digout
options.text: Dig out all the roots in autumn after harvest, sifting the soil.

options.name: competition
options.text: Plant dense cover crops and squash to shade the weeds and weed only the edges.

decision: How should the class spend its 600 trip fund?
context: A class of 24 eleven-year-olds has 600 from fundraising and can add 5 per child from the school. The trip must happen before the end of June and needs adult supervision from the two class teachers and one parent. The children have voted but the top two options tied.

options.name: museum
options.text: A hands-on science museum visit by train with a workshop booked in advance.

options.name: farmpark
options.text: A day at a working farm park with animals, a picnic and a guided tour.

options.name: outdoorday
options.text: A guided canoe and orienteering day at a nearby lake centre.

decision: Where should the florist keep unsold cut flowers overnight?
context: The shop throws away about 60 euros of roses and lilies a week. Roses last roughly seven days at 4 degrees and two days at room temperature. The shop already owns a walk-in cooler that stays about half empty.

options.name: windowdisplay
options.text: Leave them in buckets in the shop window as advertising.

options.name: backroom
options.text: Move them to the back room, which stays around 21 degrees.

options.name: coldroom
options.text: Return them to the walk-in cooler overnight and bring them out in the morning.

decision: How should we cache product pages on the web shop?
context: The shop serves about 3 million page views a month, with 12,000 products and a nightly price update at 2 am. Traffic spikes threefold during sales, and the team has two developers and a modest hosting budget of 300 a month. About 30 percent of visitors are logged in with personalised blocks.

options.name: cdnedge
options.text: Put a CDN in front with a short time-to-live and purge on product changes.

options.name: redisfrag
options.text: Cache rendered fragments in Redis and keep personalised blocks outside the cache.

options.name: fullpage
options.text: Generate static full pages for anonymous visitors after every change and serve them from disk.

options.name: httpcache
options.text: Rely on HTTP cache headers and the browser, with minimal server changes.

decision: How should the animal shelter recruit weekend volunteers?
context: The shelter needs 12 volunteers for Saturdays and Sundays and currently has five. It has a 500 per year budget for recruitment, one coordinator, and a nearby high school where students must complete service hours. About half of the previous volunteers dropped out within three months.

options.name: socialads
options.text: Run paid social media ads aimed at residents within 10 km.

options.name: schoolpartner
options.text: Partner with the high school's service-hours programme and train two student leaders.

options.name: corporatedays
options.text: Invite local companies to send teams for volunteer days.

options.name: payexpenses
options.text: Offer small expense payments to regular volunteers who commit to a set schedule.

decision: How should a mixed-ability class learn fractions?
context: A class of 28 nine-year-olds has a six-grade spread: about five pupils are well ahead and six are struggling with halves and quarters. The teacher has one assistant for two mornings a week and four weeks for the unit. Previous whole-class lessons left both ends bored or lost.

options.name: stations
options.text: Use rotating practice stations with hands-on materials and mixed-level pairs.

options.name: levelgroups
options.text: Group pupils by level and give each group different tasks while the teacher circulates.

options.name: pairwork
options.text: Pair stronger pupils with weaker ones for all activities.

options.name: wholeclass
options.text: Teach the whole class together with open-ended problems that scale in difficulty.

options.name: pullout
options.text: Pull the six struggling pupils out for daily 15-minute catch-up sessions with the assistant.

decision: How should we store 3 kg of cooked rice for tomorrow?
context: The rice was cooked at 7 pm for a lunch event the next day, and it is now 8 pm. The kitchen is 27 degrees and a large refrigerator has plenty of space. The cooks want to avoid food poisoning, which can come from bacteria that grow in rice kept warm.

options.name: roomtemp
options.text: Leave it covered on the counter overnight and reheat it before lunch.

options.name: shallowfridge
options.text: Spread it in shallow trays to cool quickly and refrigerate within an hour.

options.name: keepwarm
options.text: Keep it in the rice cooker on the warm setting overnight.

decision: Which lodging suits a family of five on the coast?
context: The family has three children aged 5, 9 and 13 and a one-week stay in August. They would like a base within walking distance of a beach in a village of 3,000 people, with a budget of about 1,800 for the week. The nearest supermarket is 4 km away, and parking is scarce in summer.

options.name: apartment
options.text: A two-bedroom apartment in the village centre with a small balcony, 1,500 for the week.

options.name: campsite
options.text: A mobile home on a campsite with a pool, a 10-minute walk from the beach, 1,300.

options.name: farmhouse
options.text: A farmhouse with a garden 5 km inland, 1,100, with a car required for the beach.

options.name: hotelfamily
options.text: A family room at a beachfront hotel with breakfast, 2,400.

options.name: guesthouse
options.text: Two rooms at a guesthouse near the harbour, 1,700.

options.name: cabin
options.text: A wooden cabin in a holiday park with its own playground, 1,650.

decision: How should the clinic reorganise its front-desk queue?
context: The clinic's lobby holds 25 people, and on Monday mornings 40 arrive within an hour. Two front-desk staff both check patients in and answer phones. Patients with urgent symptoms have waited as long as routine arrivals.

options.name: kiosk
options.text: Add two check-in kiosks and use staff for urgent-symptom questions and phones.

options.name: nurseatdoor
options.text: Station a nurse at the entrance to sort patients by urgency before check-in.

options.name: phonesplit
options.text: Move phone calls to a separate room and let desk staff handle only walk-ins.

options.name: bookedonly
options.text: Switch Mondays to appointments only, with a phone line for urgent cases.

decision: How should the team split the billing logic out of the monolith?
context: The monolith has 600,000 lines of code, and billing accounts for about 40,000 lines with its own tables and a handful of cross-calls. Six engineers work on the product, and invoicing bugs cost real revenue each month. Billing changes about twice a month, mostly for tax rules.

options.name: extractservice
options.text: Carve out billing as a separate service with its own database over the next two quarters.

options.name: leavealone
options.text: Leave it alone and put the effort into adding invoice tests.

options.name: moduleboundary
options.text: Enforce a strict internal module boundary inside the monolith with its own tests and keep a single deployment.

decision: Should the injured striker play Saturday's match?
context: The striker's physio diagnosed a grade 2 hamstring strain yesterday and estimated three weeks until a safe return. Saturday's match is a mid-table league fixture with no promotion or relegation consequences. Two other forwards are fit.

options.name: playfull
options.text: Play the full 90 minutes with tape on the leg.

options.name: playhalf
options.text: Play only the first half to limit the load.

options.name: rest
options.text: Rest and follow the physio's rehab plan, starting a fit forward instead.

options.name: painkillers
options.text: Take painkillers and start, then see how it feels.

decision: In which key should the singer perform the ballad?
context: The song's highest note in the original key is a C5, and the singer comfortably reaches an A4, with her voice cracking above that. The accompanist can transpose on sight and the performance is in two weeks at a wedding. The song's lowest note is a G3, within her comfortable range.

options.name: originalkey
options.text: Keep the original key and work on strength in her upper range.

options.name: transposedown
options.text: Transpose the accompaniment down a minor third and keep the melody otherwise unchanged.

options.name: falsettoend
options.text: Keep the original key and switch to falsetto on the top notes.

decision: How should we heat the converted garage studio this winter?
context: The studio is 28 square metres, insulated to a modest standard, and used around four hours a day by one person. Electricity costs 0.30 per kWh, the main house has a gas boiler 15 metres away, and winter lows are around minus 5. The owner wants it done before November.

options.name: electricpanel
options.text: Wall-mounted electric panel heaters, cheap to buy and install.

options.name: minisplit
options.text: A ductless mini-split heat pump with an installer quote of about 2,600.

options.name: woodstove
options.text: A small wood stove with a flue, 2,200 installed plus firewood.

options.name: oilradiator
options.text: A portable oil-filled radiator moved in when needed.

options.name: infrared
options.text: Ceiling-mounted infrared panels that warm people rather than the air.

options.name: extendcentral
options.text: Extend the house's gas central heating with a new pipe run to the studio.

decision: How should the farm shop sell this year's surplus apples?
context: The orchard produced 18 tonnes, about 5 tonnes more than the farm shop can sell fresh. A cider press operator pays modestly for juice apples, a dryer unit can be hired, and the farm has volunteers for box-packing days. Cold storage is available for about six weeks.

options.name: juicepress
options.text: Sell the surplus to the cider press and sell the cider in the shop.

options.name: boxes
options.text: Pack mixed boxes for local offices and ship them in November.

options.name: wholesaleloc
options.text: Sell the surplus in bulk to two local grocers at a lower price.

options.name: driedslices
options.text: Hire the dryer and sell dried apple slices at the shop and markets.

decision: How should the new service store user passwords?
context: The service will hold accounts for about 80,000 users and sits behind a standard web framework. The team's security checklist requires protection against offline cracking if the database leaks. Libraries for several algorithms are available and server hardware is modest.

options.name: md5hash
options.text: Hash each password with MD5 and a global salt.

options.name: sha256
options.text: Hash each password with a single round of SHA-256.

options.name: argon2
options.text: Use a memory-hard password hashing function such as Argon2id with per-user salts and tuned cost.

options.name: encrypt
options.text: Encrypt the passwords with a key stored in the config file.

options.name: plaintext
options.text: Store them as typed so that support can recover forgotten passwords.

decision: How should we fill the vacant senior role within six weeks?
context: A 40-person engineering consultancy lost its lead designer, and a major project starts in six weeks. The role would normally take 10 weeks to recruit externally and costs a recruiter 20 percent of salary. Two mid-level designers could be promoted, and a former colleague contracts at 650 a day.

options.name: promote
options.text: Promote one of the mid-level designers and backfill their role later.

options.name: recruiter
options.text: Hire a recruiter and push for a fast process, accepting a late start.

options.name: referral
options.text: Offer a large referral bonus to staff and search through personal networks.

options.name: contractor
options.text: Bring in the former colleague as a contractor until a permanent hire arrives.

decision: Which title should the memoir carry?
context: The memoir is by a retired ferry captain and covers 40 years on one island route, with humour and several storms. The editor tested five titles with 60 readers at a local book fair; the results were within a few votes of each other. The cover art shows a ferry in fog.

options.name: lastcrossing
options.text: Call it The Last Crossing, a plain title that echoes the final run of his career.

options.name: tidetimetable
options.text: Call it Tide and Timetable, a rhythmic title that stresses routine over drama.

options.name: foggyharbour
options.text: Call it Fog on the Island Route: Forty Years at the Wheel, descriptive and matching the cover art.

options.name: longasfloats
options.text: Call it As Long as She Floats, a humorous title taken from a line in chapter nine.

options.name: islandskipper
options.text: Call it Skipper of the Island: A Ferry Life, a straightforward title that names the profession.

decision: How should we route deliveries to the three islands?
context: A small grocer delivers 40 orders a week to three islands, served by ferries that run twice daily to the nearest island and once a day to the others. The grocer owns one van, the ferry fare is 22 per crossing, and a local boat operator offers a direct run for 85. Customers expect delivery within two days.

options.name: dailyferry
options.text: Send the van daily on the scheduled ferries, covering one island per day.

options.name: weeklyboat
options.text: Consolidate into two boat runs per week with the private operator.

options.name: pickuppoints
options.text: Deliver to one pick-up point per island each week and let customers collect.

options.name: islandpartner
options.text: Contract a resident on each island to deliver the last mile from a weekly bulk drop.

decision: Where should the student with low vision sit?
context: The student has corrected acuity of about 20/200 and reads best with high contrast and no glare. The whiteboard is 4 m from the front row, with windows along the left wall that cause glare after 11 am. The teacher moves around the room and uses the board for most explanations.

options.name: backrow
options.text: At the back of the room next to the door so she can leave easily.

options.name: windowseat
options.text: Next to the window, where light is best for reading.

options.name: frontcentre
options.text: Front row, centre-right, away from the window, with a desk lamp and a printed copy of board work.

options.name: rotateseats
options.text: Rotate her through different seats each week to keep things fair.

decision: How should we feed 300 people at the harvest festival?
context: The festival runs from noon to 6 pm on a village green with no kitchen, and a budget of about 1,500. Ticket prices are low, and the organisers expect crowds to peak at 1 pm and again at 4. Two volunteers have food-safety certificates.

options.name: foodtrucks
options.text: Invite three food trucks on a revenue share basis.

options.name: caterer
options.text: Hire a caterer for a fixed-price lunch buffet at 1,400.

options.name: potluck
options.text: Ask villagers to bring dishes to a communal potluck table and cook sausages on grills.

options.name: boxlunch
options.text: Pre-order boxed lunches from a bakery as part of the ticket price.

options.name: vouchers
options.text: Sell food vouchers redeemable at local cafes on the green's edge.

decision: Which front-end approach suits the internal reporting dashboard?
context: The dashboard will be used by 30 internal staff to view charts and filter tables, with data refreshed hourly. Two backend developers will build it, and one has some React experience. The company wants it live in two months and maintained by whoever is around afterwards.

options.name: react
options.text: A React single-page app with a charting library and a typed API client.

options.name: serverrender
options.text: Server-rendered pages with a few lines of JavaScript for filters.

options.name: bitool
options.text: A hosted business intelligence tool connected directly to the database.

options.name: htmxpages
options.text: Server-rendered pages with htmx-style partial updates and a small charting library.

options.name: notebook
options.text: Scheduled notebooks that publish static HTML reports each hour.

options.name: sheetsdash
options.text: A shared spreadsheet fed by a nightly export, with charts built in the sheet.

decision: What should the city build on the vacant lot beside the library?
context: The 600 square metre lot was cleared after a fire and the city owns it. Residents have asked for greenery, the library wants outdoor reading space, and nearby shops complain about a shortage of parking. The council can spend 250,000 and has to decide this quarter.

options.name: parking
options.text: A 20-space surface parking lot, the cheapest option and open within months.

options.name: pocketpark
options.text: A pocket park with trees, seating and a reading terrace attached to the library.

options.name: marketsquare
options.text: A paved square with power points for a weekly market and events.

decision: Which control is missing from the enzyme assay?
context: In a plate assay every well shows activity, including three wells that contain only buffer and substrate. Pipetting has been checked, the plate reader works, and the substrate bottle is six months old. The team wants to know whether the signal is real.

options.name: moresamples
options.text: Run more samples to increase statistical power.

options.name: noenzymeblank
options.text: Add no-enzyme blanks and a fresh-substrate control to see whether the substrate itself produces signal.

options.name: higherconc
options.text: Raise the enzyme concentration and see whether the signal scales.

options.name: repeattwice
options.text: Repeat the whole plate twice more and average the results.

decision: How should the new hedge be watered during the dry month?
context: Forty bare-root hornbeam plants went into sandy soil last week, and no rain has fallen in three weeks with none forecast for another ten days. The gardener can water in the evenings for about 20 minutes with a hose. Roots will be 20 cm deep at most this season.

options.name: dailysprinkle
options.text: Sprinkle the foliage briefly each evening.

options.name: rainonly
options.text: Rely on rain and check again in two weeks.

options.name: deepsoak
options.text: Soak the base of each plant slowly with about 10 litres twice a week and mulch the soil.

decision: How should the school clinic store vaccination records?
context: The school nurse manages records for 900 pupils, currently in paper folders in a locked cabinet. A district rule requires access during emergencies and off-site backups, and the school's IT support is one part-time person. Parents increasingly ask for digital copies.

options.name: encryptedlocal
options.text: Scan the records into an encrypted local database with nightly encrypted backups off-site.

options.name: paperonly
options.text: Keep the paper folders and photocopy them quarterly to an off-site safe.

options.name: cloudsystem
options.text: Move everything to a cloud health-records system run by a vendor.

options.name: hybridfolder
options.text: Keep paper as the master and put a summary sheet per pupil in a password-protected spreadsheet.

decision: How should the rowing crew train over the off-season?
context: The eight-person crew has 16 weeks before the spring regatta and the river is partly frozen for the first five weeks. They have an indoor ergometer room, access to a pool and a gym, and one coach available three evenings a week. Several rowers also work shifts.

options.name: ergblock
options.text: Do mostly erg sessions with a progressive intervals plan.

options.name: crosstrain
options.text: Mix swimming, running and gym work, then return to the water.

options.name: tankwork
options.text: Use a rowing tank on two evenings for technique work and the gym for strength.

options.name: campweek
options.text: Do light training and save the budget for a warm-weather training camp in week 10.

options.name: minimal
options.text: Have each rower train individually and meet as a crew only from week 6.
